findings.fix: Cross-AI lane setup: detects installed CLIs and models, proposes a review set and an execute set from the model catalog for the owner to pick, asks each role's priority order, then writes the [lanes] table of ai-kit's config.toml (per-project ./.aikit/config.toml by default, asking before replacing an existing roster). Use when the user wants to set up, refresh or check cross-AI review or execute lanes, even without the word lanes; when ai-kit-spec-review or ai-kit-spec-execute-superpowers reports no lanes exist; to find lane providers opencode no longer lists; or to migrate an old review-spec.toml. Supports --check-only, --local and --global. Not for running a review or execute with configured lanes, hand-editing one lane value, or editing [runner] or opencode.jsonc.

findings.evidence: The 442-line body holds about 9,000 tokens (6,710 words), nearly double the ~5,000-token layer-2 recommendation, and part of it is in-body duplication: the command-bearing definition at lines 420-428 restates references/config-file.md, and two NEVER rules each appear twice.
findings.fix: Point Step 4's command-bearing block at references/config-file.md instead of restating it, turn the repeated rules into pointers to their NEVER entries, and keep the question wording and gates in the body.

findings.evidence: 'Then ask policy.mode (single or double)' presents two equal options with no stated default, unlike the escalation flags (default no), the strategy question (default global-merge) and the timeout tiers (default kept).
findings.fix: State a default with an escape hatch: default to single, offering double only when the owner wants a second opinion from another vendor and a second-vendor lane is available.
